text_blocks.snippet: Both ACE inhibitors (ending in -pril) and ARBs (ending in -sartan) are equally recommended as first-line treatments for high blood pressure, but ARBs are generally preferred first because they have fewer side effects.
snippet_highlighted_words: ARBs are generally preferred first because they have fewer side effects

list.snippet: The Pathway: Both target the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) to relax blood vessels and lower blood pressure.
ACE Inhibitors: Block the enzyme that makes angiotensin II.
ARBs: Block the receptors where angiotensin II attaches.
Effectiveness: Both lower blood pressure equally well. Large studies show no major difference in preventing heart attacks or strokes between the two classes.

text_blocks.snippet: Why ARBs Are Often Chosen First (Safety & Tolerability)

list.snippet: Fewer Side Effects: Large real-world studies show patients tolerate ARBs better than ACE inhibitors.
Persistent Cough: ACE inhibitors cause a nagging, dry cough in 3% to 4% of patients due to a buildup of bradykinin. ARBs do not cause this cough.
Angioedema: ACE inhibitors carry a rare but serious risk of angioedema (deep tissue swelling of the face, lips, or tongue). ARBs have a much lower risk of this reaction.
Switching: If a patient takes an ACE inhibitor and develops the characteristic cough or swelling, doctors routinely switch them to an ARB.

text_blocks.snippet: Because they affect the same biological pathway, both drug classes share important precautions:

list.snippet: High Potassium (Hyperkalemia): Both can raise blood potassium levels, requiring lab monitoring.
Kidney Function: Both can temporarily affect kidney numbers (creatinine) and should be used with caution in severe bilateral renal artery stenosis.
Pregnancy: Both are strictly contraindicated (unsafe) in pregnancy as they can cause severe fetal harm or death.

Never Combine: Taking an ACE inhibitor and an ARB at the same time is not recommended because it sharply increases the risk of high potassium, low blood pressure, and kidney injury without added benefit.
